citation.title: Utilizing Indirect Intrapleural Pressure to Guide Mechanical Ventilation in Burn Patients With ARDS

provenance.quote: Patients less than 18 years of age, died prior to manometry placement or were designated as comfort care or withdrawal of care within 24 h of manometry placement according to advance directives or family decision, were excluded from this study.

Adult patients with severe burn injuries with or without smoke inhalation injury admitted to an ABA-verified burn center from January 2017 to May 2024 were retrospectively reviewed for those who received mechanical ventilation for greater than 48 h and developed ARDS by the Berlin definition.
Burn injured patients admitted to an ABA verified burn center that developed ARDS by the Berlin definition and received Pes were retrospectively reviewed
Ventilator settings were adjusted based on these measurements to avoid under-inflation and collapse of the alveoli at end expiration and over-inflation of the alveoli at end inspiration

the ratio of PaO2 to the fractioned of inspired oxygen (FiO2) (P/F ratio) and oxygenation indices (OI) [(FiO2 × mean airway pressure (MAP))/PaO2] were calculated to compare the severity of hypoxia prior to esophageal pressure monitoring use, and at 1, 3, and 5-day intervals following manometry initiation.
provenance.location: Methods, Data collection and analysis, p. 1257

provenance.quote: Of the 23 patients included, the median revised Baux score was 91.6 (73.9-114.6), and the mortality rate was 82.6%.
This is a retrospective review of the use of indirect intrapleural pressure measurement to guide mechanical ventilation in burn-injured patients with ARDS.
Journal of Burn Care & Research, 2025, Volume 46, Issue 6

population_description.value: Adult patients with severe burn injuries with or without smoke inhalation injury who received mechanical ventilation for greater than 48 h and developed ARDS by the Berlin definition, with worsening oxygenation despite lung protective ventilation, who underwent esophageal pressure monitoring.

provenance.quote: Adult patients with severe burn injuries with or without smoke inhalation injury admitted to an ABA-verified burn center from January 2017 to May 2024 were retrospectively reviewed for those who received mechanical ventilation for greater than 48 h and developed ARDS by the Berlin definition. Per institution protocol, patients who developed ARDS and had worsening oxygenation as determined by arterial blood gas (ABG) monitoring and oxygen saturation despite lung protective ventilation underwent esophageal pressure monitoring to further guide ventilator management.

method_verbatim.value: Waveform analysis was used to confirm that the balloon was in the lower third of the esophagus in the retrocardiac position.

provenance.quote: Waveform analysis was used to confirm that the balloon was in the lower third of the esophagus in the retrocardiac position.

position_verification.value: Waveform analysis confirming lower third of esophagus, retrocardiac position; advanced orally approximately 35-40 cm from insertion; transducer zeroed at the phlebostatic axis with patient supine at approximately 30 degrees.

provenance.quote: With the patient supine, at approximately 30°, the pressure transducer was zeroed at the phlebostatic axis. The device was advanced orally into the mid-lower third of the esophagus, a distance of approximately 35-40 cm from insertion. Waveform analysis was used to confirm that the balloon was in the lower third of the esophagus in the retrocardiac position.

method_verbatim.value: Ptp is the difference between airway pressure (Paw) and Ppl, with Pes used as a surrogate for intrapleural pressure; end-expiratory and end-inspiratory Pes obtained via hold maneuvers.

provenance.quote: Ptp is the difference between airway pressure (Paw) and Ppl ... Expiratory and inspiratory hold maneuvers were used to measure end-expiratory and plateau pressures, respectively.
provenance.location: Methods, p. 1256 (equation) and Esophageal manometry technique, p. 1256

strategy_verbatim.value: End-expiratory Pes was used to determine optimal PEEP via expiratory hold (total PEEP = set PEEP + Auto-PEEP; Δ-PEEP = Optimal PEEP − Total PEEP); end-inspiratory Pes used to calculate a safe plateau pressure threshold: Safe Pplateau = 20 cmH2O + Pes.

provenance.quote: End-expiratory Pes was used to determine optimal PEEP. First, an expiratory hold maneuver was performed by the ventilator to determine the total PEEP in the patient. ... Δ −PEEP = Optimal PEEP −Total PEEP ... Safe Pplateau = 20 cmH2O + Pes.

titration_frequency.value: Upon insertion to establish baseline, then every 24 h or following significant events

provenance.quote: Generally, values were obtained upon insertion of the esophageal manometry device to establish baseline values to guide ventilator observations and changes. Additional measurements were obtained every 24 h afterwards or following significant events, such as ventilator changes, operative interventions, changes in patient positioning, and after wound care was performed.

plateau_or_ptp_ceiling.value: Safe Pplateau = 20 cmH2O + Pes (delta pressure threshold of 15-20 cmH2O above the Pes at inspiratory hold)

provenance.quote: With the chest wall contribution defined as approximately 10 cmH2O, this translated to a delta pressure threshold of 15-20 cmH2O above the Pes at inspiratory hold and represented the maximum plateau pressure that could be safely met with ventilator adjustments.

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ards_only: ARDS by Berlin definition was an inclusion criterion. obesity_subgroup: no BMI reported. timing_subgroup: Pes placed after worsening ARDS despite lung protective ventilation but no interval from a reference event is reported, so early/late cannot be coded. ptp_target_subgroups: end-expiratory Pes used to set optimal PEEP via absolute subtraction, but the numeric end-expiratory Ptp target for this cohort is not stated (the −2 to +2 cmH2O range is cited as EPVent-2 background), so coded unclear.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: No overlap. This report is not listed in any COHORTS.md cluster. Single-center retrospective cohort at the MedStar Washington Hospital Center burn center (Washington, DC), enrolment January 2017 to May 2024, burn-ARDS population; no trial registration reported; no shared cohort with the EPVent, Mannheim, MGH lung rescue, or Angers clusters.
unclear_items: design.n_centers: single center stated in Discussion ('single-center retrospective study') but the number of centres is not given as a figure; coded single.
design.countries: country inferred from the institution address (MedStar Washington Hospital Center, Washington, DC, United States); not stated as the study country.
feasibility.n_placement_successful: derived — the paper says all 28 underwent Pes monitoring but does not report placement success/failure explicitly.
intervention.peep_titration_target.strategy: the numeric end-expiratory Ptp target applied in this cohort is not stated; the −2 to +2 cmH2O range is cited as EPVent-2 background, so coded 'other'.
outcomes (oxygenation index) dispersion: Table 4 reports pre OI SEM 1.93 while the Abstract and Results text report 1.92 for the same value; Table 4 used as authoritative.

population.additional_baseline (Etiology of burn): Table 1 row reads 'Etiology of burn, n (%) 3 (13.0)' with subgroups Flame 19 (82.6), Scald 2 (8.7), Flash/other 2 (8.7); the 3 (13.0) header value does not match the subgroups and appears to be a typographical error; subgroups recorded as printed.
outcomes (Resolution of ARDS): text states 'nine patients (35%)' while Table 2 reports 9 (39.1%); 9/23 = 39.1%, so the 35% in text appears erroneous; Table 2 value recorded.
subgroup_flags.timing_subgroup: no interval from intubation, ICU admission, or ARDS onset to Pes placement is reported.
design.randomised: coded false as a retrospective study; the paper does not state 'not randomised' explicitly.
extraction_flags.general_notes: Within-patient before/after design: same 23 patients studied at current PEEP before Pes and at Pes-guided optimal PEEP afterwards; paired contrasts recorded in paired_effects. PEEP data are mean (SD) (Table 3); P/F and OI are least square means (SEM) from a mixed-effect model (Table 4); clinical outcomes are median (IQR) (Table 2). The 5 patients who died within 48 h of Pes monitoring were excluded from analysis, so n_analysed = 23 of 28 monitored. No balloon-related complications reported either way. No trial registration reported.
